text:
kevin: Heads-up — we hit severe backpressure on audit-ingest this morning when a customer ramped up event volume. CPUs spiked, KMS latencies ballooned, and the ES indexing queue started falling behind. Anyone seen similar patterns?

maria: yep saw the alerts. root cause seems to be a recent RBAC change that upped tenant-level verbose logging + an on-demand report job. combined with small single-event KMS decrypts = lots of round trips.

aj: curious numbers? how many KMS calls/sec and what was the batching config?

kevin: short summary: ~18k audit events/s for ~7m sec-aggregated window. KMS calls peaked ~14k/s. current batcher config: 1-2 items per batch (worst), flush_ms=50. ES indexing backlog grew to 30m docs.

zara: that flush_ms is too low for the traffic shape. we should increase batching_threshold and max_wait to reduce per-event overhead. also consider envelope encryption so we don't call KMS for each event.

maria: +1 on envelope encryption. security concern: we need to ensure DEK caching TTL aligns with rotation policy. proposed: cache DEKs in memcache with 10m TTL, refresh on miss, use KMS only for DEK unwrap. reduces calls by ~95%.

aj: that helps cost/latency but adds blowup risk if a DEK is compromised. what's our mitigation?

security-bot: Note: DEK caching requires design doc and threat assessment. See policy: https://redwood.internal/security/crypto-guidelines. :shield:

kevin: tradeoffs recognized. alternative short-term: tenant-level sampling for verbose customers + backpressure circuit on per-tenant queue. if tenant exceeds token_budget or queue_time > 200ms, we sample 1% of verbose events and mark the rest with sampling metadata. customers see an explicit sampling flag.

maria: customer-facing validation: any sampling must be communicated and visible in audit events, i.e., {"sampled": true, "original_count": 1000}. product/legal needs to sign off for regulated tenants.

zara: on ES side, index mapping: change to time-partitioned indices, move large JSON blobs to blob-store (S3) and store pointers in ES to reduce indexing cost. also switch heavy fields to keyword analyzers only when needed.

aj: ops ops — can we change batching config via feature flag per deployment? need canary before global change.

sre-oncall: yes, we already have a dynamic batching flag in k8s configmap: AUDIT_BATCHER_CONFIG. canary rollout across one dedicated shard. use these knobs: "batch_max_items": 500, "batch_max_ms": 200, "per_tenant_qos": true.

kevin: quick config snippet for experiment:

```
AUDIT_BATCHER_CONFIG = {
  "batch_max_items": 250,
  "batch_max_ms": 120,
  "max_batch_bytes": 4_194_304,
  "per_tenant_queue_limit": 5000
}
```

maria: also enable KV cache for recent tenant DEKs: DEK_CACHE_TTL=600. add strict telemetry: per-tenant KMS calls/sec metric + billing tags so finance can attribute incremental cost.

zara: reminder: any change that affects encryption flow needs an e2e test for rotation and replay. add post-deploy validation that checks 1) events decrypted correctly 2) sampling flags propagate to customer API and 3) ES pointer integrity.

aj: about vuln triage — we also got an alert for a libcrypto CVE in a transitive dep. low severity but we should patch in next minor and ensure our KMS fallback path is tested.

security-bot: Vulnerability ticket created: SEC-2026-1123. Patch scheduled for 48h.

sre-oncall: incident plan: for immediate relief we can 1) enable tenant-sampling for top 5 verbose tenants, 2) increase batching thresholds, 3) temporarily route verbose customers to a slower warm path with daily rollup export.

kevin: documentation ask: we need a customer-facing note and an internal runbook that explains sampling, encryption caching, and the repro/mitigation steps. will draft and share.

maria: I'll open a PR with the canary config + DEK caching implementation + runbook link.

zara: tl;dr: reduce KMS calls (envelope + DEK cache), increase batching, per-tenant QoS and sampling, ES pointer strategy, canary rollout, and legal signoff for regulated tenants. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks. assigning follow-ups: @maria -> PR + runbook, @zara -> ES mapping proposal, @aj -> vuln patch validation, @sre-oncall -> canary rollout plan. I'll ping product/legal for customer communication.

maria: noted. writing up action items now.

kevin: we'll sync tomorrow 10:30 PT in eng-security channel.
